target_customer: Operators of commercial drone services (maritime delivery, inspection, aerial data capture) who wanted drones to run unattended from fixed sites
problem: Commercial drones needed a pilot and manual battery changes for every mission. Airmada built an enclosed ground station that stores the drone, swaps batteries and launches missions automatically.
business_model: hardware ground stations sold or leased to drone operators, with early focus on small maritime deliveries at about $300 per trip
product_category: autonomous drone ground station (drone in a box)

founders.name: Dan Danay
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch (Mar 2016) describe him as an ex-Israeli naval officer and Sloan graduate. His other roles on the page (Check Point, keyTango) are later or undated and not recorded as prior.

founders.name: Boris Lipchin
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch (Mar 2016) and CTO on the YC page; no background given.

competitors.name: Airobotics
competitors.what: Israeli maker of a fully automated drone base (Airbase) with robotic battery and payload swap
competitors.traction_then: beta trials with Israel Chemicals, which then signed as launch customer
competitors.funding_then: reported $28.5M by New Atlas (article date not verified)

technical_complexity.rationale: A weatherproof enclosure with reliable robotic battery swap, autonomous launch and landing and remote operation was hard for a two-person hardware team, and beta tests ran in Panama, Estonia and Iceland per TechCrunch.

defensibility.rationale: No patents or exclusive customers are reported in sources. Several rivals built similar docks in the same period.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Airobotics unveiled a similar fully automated base in June 2016. Later large vendors such as DJI sold docks, but no source ties them to Airmada. The company is recorded as ceased operations without a date.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Mar 2016) reports beta tests in three countries and delivery signups opened in Panama, with a claimed delivery cost of about $300 per trip versus launch boats at roughly twice that. No revenue is reported.

branding.domain_note: Used airmada.com per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: The name evokes a fleet of drones and got TechCrunch and trade coverage around Demo Day, but no source describes a logo, community or brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Airmada was an MIT-born two-founder startup building automated drone ground stations, with beta tests in three countries by March 2016 and about $870K of reported funding across rounds from YC, Dorm Room Fund, Project 11 and FoundersX. CB Insights and Dealroom record that it ceased operations, but no date or cause is public, so no failure factors are assigned.
